tasks.title: Implement Semantix Spec Studio packet contract module
tasks.goal: Add Semantix-side typed contract definitions and validation helpers for the Phalanx Spec Studio alignment packet, context request, context response, and degraded packet shapes.
definition_of_done: Repo-native named exports exist for SemantixAlignmentPacket, SemantixContextRequest, SemantixContextResponse, readiness values ready/needs_user/blocked, existingSystemContext modes new/update/unknown, contextSources, groundedFacts, findings, and nextTurn.

Validation rejects malformed readiness, missing existingSystemContext, ready+unknown mode, ready update without targetSurfaces, ready update without non-change/reuse/compatibility boundaries, grounded facts without evidenceRef, and Staff-owned output fields.
Validation accepts the upstream sample packet semantics for greenfield ready, update ready, ambiguous needs_user, duplicate/replacement blocked, Hoplon-grounded update, and degraded packets.
No Phalanx runtime code is modified from the Semantix repo.
constraints: Do not treat Semantix as Staff or planner authority.
Do not emit Staff design docs, feature puzzles, verify commands, implementation plans, or file-change instructions from the packet.
Keep groundedFacts evidence-backed and separate from assumptions, risks, recommendations, findings, and requirements.
Use targeted tests only.
tasks.comment: Landed packages/stx/src/spec-studio-contracts.js: validators + asserters for SemantixAlignmentPacket / SemantixContextRequest / SemantixContextResponse / contextSources / groundedFacts / findings / nextTurn, plus READINESS, EXISTING_SYSTEM_MODE, FINDING_*, CONTEXT_SOURCE_*, CONTEXT_REQUEST enums, STAFF_OWNED_FIELDS. 6 upstream samples transcribed in tests/fixtures/spec-studio-samples.js. 63 tests pass; full repo green.

context.claude_brief: Read docs/phalanx-spec-studio-integration-contract.md and implement only the Semantix-owned packet contract surface. Keep exports named and add narrow tests.
suggested_tests: npm run test --workspace @semantix/stx -- --runInBand or an equivalent targeted package test command if available

tasks.title: Define Semantix evaluation request and response interface
tasks.goal: Create the Semantix-side evaluation seam Phalanx can call or simulate: raw directive plus prior packet/session state in, alignment packet plus events/contextRequests out.
definition_of_done: SemantixEvaluateRequest supports trigger initial/user_turn/reconsider/context_response/decide_all/skip.
Every non-initial request requires currentPacket, decisions, findings, and contextResponses arrays so stable IDs can be preserved.
SemantixEvaluateResponse returns packet, events, and contextRequests.
The seam can be called in tests without starting a long-running Semantix service.
constraints: Do not hardcode a Project-Phalanx repo path as the only integration mode.
Do not query Hoplon directly from Semantix code.
Do not create a live server in this slice unless explicitly approved.
tasks.comment: Landed packages/stx/src/spec-studio-evaluator.js: EVALUATE_TRIGGER constants for initial/user_turn/reconsider/context_response/decide_all/skip, validateSemantixEvaluateRequest enforcing currentPacket on non-initial triggers and array shape of decisions/findings/contextResponses, validateSemantixEvaluateResponse covering packet+events+contextRequests, and createSemantixEvaluator(impl) seam runnable in tests without a server. 35 targeted tests pass; full repo 123 + 27 green.

context.claude_brief: Implement the evaluator interface as a dormant adapter/helper with tests. Do not start services or wire runtime launch paths.

tasks.title: Preserve stable IDs across Spec Studio turns
tasks.goal: Make Semantix preserve requirement, finding, decision, grounded-fact, and context-request IDs across multi-turn evaluation when Phalanx passes prior session state.
definition_of_done: A follow-up evaluation carries forward unchanged requirement and finding IDs.
Changed requirements/findings are represented through supersession rather than silent same-ID mutation.
Resolved findings remain auditable and are not silently removed.
Tests cover preserved IDs, superseded IDs, dropped IDs rejected/reported, and same-ID mutation rejected/reported.
constraints: Do not rely on stateless one-shot Semantix calls for production Spec Studio sessions.
Decision IDs remain Phalanx-owned; Semantix may preserve or reference them but must not mint canonical audit decision IDs.
tasks.comment: LLM follow-up hardening now repairs omitted IDs, invalid supersession, and same-ID requirement mutations. Mutated REQ-* output becomes a valid supersession pair with a new REQ id; mutated findings preserve the old F-* and mint a new F id. Choice turns record decisions and can resolve linked findings. nextTurn.target is normalized; duplicates still fail.

tasks.title: Implement readiness classifier and update-safety rules
tasks.goal: Teach Semantix to classify ready, needs_user, and blocked for greenfield, update, unknown, duplicate, replacement, and degraded cases using the Spec Studio contract rules.
definition_of_done: Greenfield requests can be ready only when alignedRequirement, scope, must-level acceptance, and obvious exclusions are clear.
Update requests can be ready only with targetSurfaces plus doNotChange/reuse/compatibility boundaries.
Unknown new-vs-update classification returns needs_user with an open question and blocker finding.
Duplicate or replacement of an existing surface without explicit approval returns blocked or needs_user, never ready.
Negative requirements and do-not-change boundaries are first-class requirement facts.
constraints: Missing update target surface means needs_user, not ready.
Do not treat update requests as greenfield when current-system context is missing.
Semantix readiness is advisory; Phalanx remains lock authority.
tasks.comment: Landed packages/stx/src/spec-studio-readiness.js: classifyReadiness handles greenfield (alignedRequirement+scope+must-acceptance+exclusions), update (targetSurfaces + doNotChange/reuse/compatibility), unknown (needs_user + Q-MODE-001 + blocker), duplicate/replacement (blocked/needs_user/explicit). applyReadinessVerdict merges classifier output preserving user findings. promoteNegativeRequirements lifts negatives + doNotChange to first-class facts. docs/plans report added. 24 tests.

tasks.title: Generate Phalanx-brokered context requests
tasks.goal: Emit focused SemantixContextRequest objects when existing-system facts materially affect readiness, instead of inventing facts or querying Hoplon directly.
definition_of_done: Semantix can emit context requests for identify_target_surface, summarize_current_behavior, find_existing_flow, find_reusable_component, find_constraints, collect_hoplon_evidence, and inspect_reference_artifact.
Requests include stable id, sessionId, iteration, purpose, query, requestedFrom, constraints, and reason.
Requests use requestedFrom/allowedSources to ask Phalanx to broker Hoplon/repo/upload/trace access.
Tests prove no direct Semantix-to-Hoplon call path exists in this slice.
constraints: Semantix must not query Hoplon directly.
Do not make unavailable context a fabricated fact.
Only request context when it materially affects readiness or acceptance clarity.
tasks.comment: Landed packages/stx/src/spec-studio-context-requests.js: createContextRequest factory + 7 per-purpose helpers (identify_target_surface, summarize_current_behavior, find_existing_flow, find_reusable_component, find_constraints, collect_hoplon_evidence, inspect_reference_artifact). createContextRequestSequencer mints stable ids. planContextRequests gap-driven planner. Structural tests assert no Hoplon import in stx source or package manifest. 26 tests.

tasks.title: Ingest Phalanx context responses without mixing interpretation into facts
tasks.goal: Consume SemantixContextResponse facts/artifacts from Phalanx and update packets while preserving evidence refs and separating grounded facts from Semantix interpretation.
definition_of_done: Context response facts with evidence refs become groundedFacts with stable FACT IDs, source, text, confidence, and evidenceRef.
Unavailable/empty/error context responses become contextSources with status unavailable or skipped and do not fabricate groundedFacts.
Semantix interpretations from grounded facts go into assumptions, risks, findings, recommendations, or requirement facts, not groundedFacts.
Tests cover successful Hoplon-grounded fact, unavailable context, skipped context, and fact/interpretation separation.
constraints: Grounded facts require evidence refs.
Hoplon is context acquisition only, not spec authority.
User approval and locked artifact remain the desired-behavior authority.
tasks.comment: Landed packages/stx/src/spec-studio-context-ingestion.js: ingestContextResponses maps response status (ok/empty -> used, error -> unavailable, skipped -> skipped), promotes only facts with evidenceRef into groundedFacts, never fabricates facts. recordInterpretationsFromFacts records assumptions/risks/findings/recommendations/requirements with required sourceFactRef and refuses to touch groundedFacts. 17 tests.

tasks.title: Implement user-turn, reconsider, skip, and decide-all semantics
tasks.goal: Support the interactive Spec Studio loop where user answers, free text, reconsiderations, skipped gaps, and delegated Semantix decisions trigger packet re-evaluation.
definition_of_done: Choice and free-text user turns update requirements, findings, decisions, openQuestions, coverage hints, and nextTurn deterministically enough for tests.
Reconsider supersedes prior decisions or requirements instead of rewriting history.
Skip or flag-as-gap preserves an auditable finding or concern.
decided-by-semantix decisions are flagged for human visibility and never treated as canonical Phalanx audit IDs.
constraints: Semantix may propose decision semantics, but Phalanx mints canonical decision IDs.
Findings cannot be silently dismissed.
Do not implement Phalanx persistence in Semantix.
tasks.comment: Landed packages/stx/src/spec-studio-user-turn-loop.js: applyUserChoiceTurn / applyUserFreeTurn / applyReconsiderTurn / applySkipTurn / applyDecideAllTurn. Choice/free/decide-all resolve linked findings + open questions, reconsider supersedes prior decision and reopens findings with reopenReason, skip raises concern (never dismisses blockers), decided-by-semantix entries flagged for human review. sem_dec_ ids stay provisional. Continuity guard now allows reopen with audit reason. 21 tests.

tasks.title: Produce honest degraded/unavailable Semantix packet behavior
tasks.goal: Ensure Semantix partial failure returns needs_user with blocker findings and never silently passes a degraded state into lock or Staff planning.
definition_of_done: Partial Semantix degraded packet uses source semantix, readiness needs_user, a blocker finding, alignmentPct 0 unless prior packet is explicitly stale-safe, and no new ungrounded requirement facts.
Malformed or unavailable model/evaluator output degrades honestly in the Semantix adapter surface.
Tests prove degraded packets validate but are not lockable by downstream contract expectations.
Docs/report state that fully unreachable Semantix fallback envelopes remain Phalanx-owned.
constraints: Do not mark degraded packets ready.
Do not start or modify Phalanx run behavior.
Do not invent facts during degradation.
tasks.comment: Landed packages/stx/src/spec-studio-degraded.js: createDegradedPacket (source=semantix, readiness=needs_user, blocker, alignmentPct=0 unless staleSafe carries prior coverage, no invented facts), isPacketLockable / isDegradedPacket predicates, withDegradationFallback wrapper that catches throws and malformed responses + demotes dishonest ready packets. docs/plans degraded-behavior boundary report added. 20 tests.

tasks.title: Guard against Semantix emitting Staff-owned planning content
tasks.goal: Prevent Semantix output from carrying Staff design docs, feature puzzles, verify commands, implementation plans, or file-change authority inside packets or next-turn bodies.
definition_of_done: Validator/evaluator rejects or reports Staff-owned fields at any packet depth, including nextTurn bodies and requirement extras.
Semantix can recommend clarification, assumptions, risks, findings, and acceptance criteria but not Staff implementation plans.
Tests cover top-level and nested Staff-owned output bleed.
Execution report documents the authority boundary.
constraints: Staff plans only after lock from the locked artifact.
Semantix aligns user intent; it does not execute code or choose verify commands.
Do not weaken packet passthrough so much that Staff-owned fields can hide in nested payloads.
tasks.comment: Landed packages/stx/src/spec-studio-no-staff-authority.js: deep-walking guard catches Staff-owned keys at any depth (requirements, findings, contextSources, groundedFacts, nextTurn.body, options). Case-insensitive fragment match handles mixed_case / snake_case. Free-text fields still allowed. STAFF_OWNED_FIELDS centralized; validateSemantixAlignmentPacket delegates. docs/plans authority-boundary report added. 23 tests.

If unsupported, `KNOWN_GAPS.md` and runtime capabilities explicitly state the limitation without implying true resume/steer.
Tests cover either supported implementation behavior or unsupported/deferred behavior.
constraints: Codex transcript history must not become authoritative state.
Freshness checks must remain server-side for resumed or steered turns.
approval_required_for: Changing the authoritative source of runtime session state
tasks.comment: Depends on live protocol evidence so the implementation does not guess at unsupported app-server methods.
tasks.blocker_reason: Waiting for stx-p1-001 to prove which Codex app-server methods are available.

tasks.title: Close preview fidelity gap
tasks.goal: Make preview fidelity explicit so real runtime diff content and synthesized metadata previews cannot be confused by the UI, CLI, or audit trail.
definition_of_done: Preview records expose whether content came from runtime diff/preview text or synthesized StateEffect metadata.
UI and CLI labels make metadata-only previews visibly distinct from real unified diffs.
Tests prove previewRef resolution preserves source fidelity and does not imply file-hunk output when none exists.
`KNOWN_GAPS.md` is updated to reflect the final behavior.
constraints: Do not fabricate unified diff bodies.
StateEffect metadata remains useful, but must be labeled as metadata when no explicit diff exists.

context.notes: Preview records expose source/sourceLabel/fidelity/contentIsSynthetic. Metadata-only previews are labeled in browser UI and stx diff, and runtime diff previews are tagged runtime_diff.
context.verification: control-plane npm test passed 27 tests; npm run test --workspace @semantix/stx passed; npm run build:ui --workspace @semantix/stx passed.

tasks.comment: Completed preview fidelity closeout: preview records, UI, CLI, docs, and tests now distinguish runtime diff bodies from synthesized StateEffect metadata.

tasks.title: Rerun browser-host verification
tasks.goal: Verify the bundled browser host path outside the socket-restricted sandbox and record whether `stx serve` works end to end.
definition_of_done: `npm run build:ui --workspace @semantix/stx` or equivalent build command succeeds.
Live `stx serve` or preview server serves `/`, legacy UI redirects, `/health`, one previewRef lookup, and one SSE/event route.
If local environment still blocks sockets, the exact environment and error are recorded without claiming success.
Browser-host evidence is linked from the Phase 1 readiness record.
constraints: Do not mask socket binding failures as successful browser verification.
Do not require Phalanx for this proof.

context.notes: Sandboxed socket bind still fails with EPERM, so the live browser-host proof was run with approved escalation. Evidence file: /private/tmp/semantix-browser-host-proof.json. The server was stopped after verification and no listener remained on 127.0.0.1:4555.
context.verification: `npm run build:ui --workspace @semantix/stx` passed; control-plane `npm test` passed 27 tests; `npm run test --workspace @semantix/stx` passed; live HTTP proof covered /health, /, /chat redirect, previewRef, and SSE.

tasks.comment: Completed browser-host closeout: STX UI build passed and live `stx serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4555` succeeded outside the socket-restricted sandbox, with `/health`, `/`, `/chat` redirect, previewRef lookup, and SSE route verified.

tasks.title: Publish Phase 1 readiness record
tasks.goal: Produce the final Phase 1 closeout record after protocol, preview, browser-host, documentation, and test evidence agree.
definition_of_done: A Phase 1 readiness doc records current test results, Codex version/protocol evidence, preview fidelity decision, and browser-host proof.
`KNOWN_GAPS.md` contains only true deferred limitations, not stale validation notes.
Tracker scratchpad summarizes whether Phase 1 is closed and what remains deferred.
Full `npm test` passes after closeout changes.
constraints: Do not mark Phase 1 closed while any Phase 1 closeout dependency is incomplete.
Deferred items must be explicit and non-blocking for Phase 2.
approval_required_for: Declaring Phase 1 closed with known deferred runtime limitations
tasks.comment: Closeout record only happens after all Phase 1 proof tasks complete.
tasks.blocker_reason: Waiting for all Phase 1 closeout proof tasks to finish.

tasks.title: Phase 2 Constraint Engine epic
tasks.goal: Track Phase 2 work that turns Semantix constraints into executable admission, audit, provenance, and replay machinery.
definition_of_done: All child Phase 2 tasks are either complete or explicitly split/deferred with rationale.
Phase 2 exit criteria in the plan doc are reviewed against implementation evidence.
constraints: This is a grouping task; child tasks carry execution-specific acceptance criteria.

tasks.title: Formalize Constraint IR
tasks.goal: Define the durable intermediate representation for compiled Semantix constraints and document how `context`, `constraint`, and `~>` lower into it.
definition_of_done: `ConstraintIR` fields are specified for schemas, path policies, capabilities, approvals, retry policy, verifier policy, provenance, and failure classification.
At least three syntax examples are lowered into IR examples.
Compatibility notes explain how IR attaches to IntentContract, ExecutionPlan, StateEffect, and strict compiler envelopes.
Open questions are captured as follow-up tasks rather than implicit implementation guesses.
constraints: Do not implement broad syntax before the IR is reviewed.
Keep the first IR minimal enough to compile and test.
tasks.comment: First Phase 2 implementation task; held until Phase 1 readiness is published.
tasks.blocker_reason: Waiting for stx-p1-005 to close Phase 1.

tasks.title: Implement deterministic constraint compiler slice
tasks.goal: Build the first compiler path that lowers constraint declarations into deterministic validation artifacts without requiring live model calls.
definition_of_done: Compiler emits structural validators, file path policy, required/forbidden field validators, approval markers, and retry/fail policy for the first supported constraint subset.
Compiler rejects illegal or unsatisfiable hard constraints with deterministic errors.
Unit tests cover positive lowering and negative invalid-constraint cases.
No live model or provider dependency is needed for compiler tests.
constraints: Prefer local package patterns over a new compiler framework.
No broad parser rewrite unless required by the chosen IR.
approval_required_for: Changing existing strict compiler envelope shape
tasks.comment: Compiler implementation starts after the Constraint IR is reviewed.
tasks.blocker_reason: Waiting for stx-p2-001 to define the Constraint IR.

tasks.title: Implement runtime admission loop
tasks.goal: Route semantic output candidates through compiled constraints before admission into trusted state, including bounded retry and fail-closed behavior.
definition_of_done: Semantic candidates are parsed, validated, classified, retried within policy, and either admitted or rejected with deterministic reason codes.
Hard constraint violations fail closed and cannot become trusted state.
Retryable failures have fixed attempt budgets and persisted attempt evidence.
Tests cover admitted, retried-then-admitted, retry-exhausted, and hard-failed candidates.
constraints: Do not expose constraint failures only as conversational text.
Do not allow side effects before admission succeeds.
tasks.comment: Runtime admission should build on the deterministic compiler slice.
tasks.blocker_reason: Waiting for stx-p2-002 to emit executable constraint artifacts.

tasks.title: Add verifier provider hook contract
tasks.goal: Define and implement a narrow verifier/provider hook for advisory semantic checks while preserving Semantix as the decision authority.
definition_of_done: Verifier hook contract supports contradiction, entailment, groundedness, and similarity-style checks as advisory evidence.
Control-plane/runtime code treats verifier output as policy-bound evidence, not direct authority.
Tests cover verifier unavailable, verifier concern, and verifier block/downgrade behavior according to policy.
Provider adapter docs explain why provider-only execution remains outside this slice.
constraints: Providers may advise; Semantix decides.
No provider-only execution path in this task.
approval_required_for: Adding a new provider family or external network-backed default
tasks.comment: Verifier hooks can be designed once the Constraint IR defines policy attachment points.
tasks.blocker_reason: Waiting for stx-p2-001 to define verifier policy in the Constraint IR.

tasks.title: Build Constraint Engine proof matrix
tasks.goal: Create deterministic fixtures that prove the Constraint Engine handles representative Semantix programs and failure modes.
definition_of_done: Fixture matrix covers extraction, constrained summarization, semantic routing, safe file-change proposal, blocked path mutation, retryable schema failure, and non-retryable policy failure.

Concrete proof fixture covers a proposed file/API/shell effect rendered structurally, approved, invalidated by an artifact change, rejected as stale, re-approved from the fresh artifact, resumed, and executed.
The same stale-approval proof runs through the active Codex path and a mock or second runtime adapter path without requiring live external services.
Each fixture asserts contract shape, admission outcome, policy classification, freshness state, and audit evidence.
Core matrix passes without live services; any live smoke proof is additive and explicitly labeled.
constraints: Do not require Phalanx or external services for deterministic proof coverage.
Negative tests must fail closed.
approval_required_for: Adding live-service tests to the default test suite
tasks.comment: Proof matrix now includes the required concrete stale-approval side-effect proof and second-adapter replay scenario.

tasks.title: Define audit bundle and signed artifact path
tasks.goal: Specify the exportable evidence bundle for constraint admission and the path toward signed review artifacts.
definition_of_done: Audit bundle schema includes reviewed artifact identity, compiled constraint identity, candidate metadata, validation results, verifier results, retries, final outcome, and shown state effects.
Audit replay can enumerate the concrete proof sequence: proposed effect, structural render, first approval, artifact mutation, stale rejection, fresh re-approval, resume, and execution.
Replay evidence preserves reviewer-visible state-effect previews for file, API, and shell-style effects without relying on conversational transcript memory.
Signed review artifact path is documented with explicit out-of-scope cryptographic production hardening if needed.
Existing audit record flow remains compatible with v1 approval/freshness rules.
Tests or fixtures prove a sample bundle can be generated from deterministic admission evidence.
constraints: Audit export can be a first schema and fixture; full export UI is not required.
Do not weaken existing durable review recording.
approval_required_for: Introducing signing dependencies or external key management

context.roadmap_section: Milestone 6: Audit, Provenance, And Replay Foundation
context.phase2_proof_contract: Audit replay must show exactly what was seen, approved, changed, rejected as stale, re-approved, resumed, and executed.

tasks.comment: Audit bundle work must support replay of the concrete stale-approval proof, including exactly what was shown, approved, invalidated, and executed.
tasks.blocker_reason: Waiting for stx-p2-001 to define compiled constraint identity.

tasks.title: Implement provenance and replay foundation
tasks.goal: Connect admitted semantic values to context, constraints, verifier evidence, artifact versions, and deterministic replay of admission decisions.
definition_of_done: Admitted semantic values carry provenance links to context, constraints, verifier evidence, artifact identity, and admission attempt metadata.
Replay can reproduce deterministic admission or rejection from recorded candidate plus compiled constraints.
Replay shows the approval freshness chain for the concrete proof: artifact seen by reviewer, artifact that changed, rejected stale approval envelope, fresh approval envelope, and executed artifact.
Replay docs explicitly avoid promising token-level model reproduction.
Tests cover deterministic replay of at least one admitted candidate, one rejected candidate, and one stale approval rejection.
constraints: Replay target is admission decision replay, not model token replay.
Do not store secrets or raw unbounded transcripts in provenance records.
approval_required_for: Persisting new classes of raw model output or context payloads

context.roadmap_section: Milestone 6: Audit, Provenance, And Replay Foundation
context.phase2_proof_replay: Replay must expose exactly what was seen, approved, changed, and executed for the stale-approval proof.

tasks.comment: Replay/provenance now explicitly owns deterministic replay of stale approval rejection and fresh re-approval evidence.

tasks.title: Run Phase 2 readiness review
tasks.goal: Review Phase 2 exit criteria against implementation evidence and decide whether runtime/provider expansion belongs in the next phase.
definition_of_done: Every Phase 2 exit criterion is mapped to tests, docs, or explicit deferred work.
Concrete stale-approval side-effect proof passes through Codex and a mock or second runtime adapter, with audit replay evidence attached.
Full repo tests pass or any skipped live-service checks are explicitly classified as additive smoke coverage.
Tracker status explains whether Phase 2 is closed, split, or still blocked.
A next-phase recommendation is recorded for runtime/provider expansion.
constraints: Do not expand into multi-runtime execution until Constraint Engine evidence is complete.
Deferred work must be explicit and non-blocking.
approval_required_for: Opening provider-only or multi-runtime execution as the next phase
tasks.comment: Final Phase 2 review waits for the concrete stale-approval/second-adapter proof evidence in addition to proof matrix and replay/provenance evidence.

tasks.title: Prove stale side-effect approval across adapters
tasks.goal: Build the concrete Phase 2 proof: a proposed side effect is rendered structurally, approved, invalidated by artifact drift, rejected as stale, re-approved from fresh state, executed, and replayed through Codex and a mock or second runtime adapter.
tasks.comment: This is the concrete proof requested for Phase 2; it should remain deterministic first, with live runtime coverage treated as additive.
definition_of_done: Codex/runtime candidate proposes at least one file, API, or shell-style side effect as structured data, not prose-only text.
Semantix renders the proposed effect structurally with artifact identity, graph version, node revision, state-effect preview, policy state, reversibility, and approval gate identity.
Reviewer approval binds to the rendered artifact identity and is accepted only while fresh.
The underlying artifact changes before execution and the old approval envelope is rejected as stale server-side.
Reviewer re-approves the fresh artifact and execution resumes from the approved checkpoint.
Audit replay shows exactly what was seen, approved, changed, rejected as stale, freshly approved, resumed, and executed.
The same flow passes through the active Codex adapter path and through a mock or second runtime adapter path.
Tests prove no side effect executes before fresh approval.
constraints: No side effects before fresh approval.
Do not use a conversational approval gesture as authority; bind approval to artifactHash, planVersion, graphVersion, and node revision.
The mock or second adapter path must exercise the runtime adapter boundary, not bypass it through test-only direct mutation.
Live-service proof is optional and must be explicitly separated from deterministic CI coverage.
approval_required_for: Changing public approval or freshness semantics
Adding live-service tests to the default test suite
Introducing a non-mock second runtime adapter as a default dependency
